The Omnissiah’s Embrace – Part 2
- By Ryan Jones

For the first time he could remember, Archmagos Dominus Belisarius Cawl heard nothing but silence.

Cogitators whirred, nearby servo-skulls could be heard faintly humming through the corridors and the background magnificent machinery of Mars ever churned, but Cawl heard none of it.

For a moment, everything stopped.

Cawl could pin it down to the exact zeptosecond Thulia’s sacred robes laid bare on the floor. The same ones that appeared on the floor just a few metres in front of him. Still frozen, he accessed his memory banks to reassure himself what he just saw wasn’t a dream.

A frame forever frozen within the Archmagos’ mind was Thulia’s form as she crossed the threshold of the door, glimpsed once but forever engraved in the memory banks of the Archmagos.

He was alive.

Waves of golden red pieced through the ancient tapestries draped throughout the walkway, emanating towards the doorway, drawing him in. The burning of motor oil through the forge-city was thick in the air, enraging and disorientating. Compelled, lost of motor function Cawl stumbled forwards, trembling.

Despite Cawl’s natural form being long ago replaced by cybernetic augmentations his senses were overwhelmed. Heart thumping in his ears, nearby candescence blinded him as ancient raw industrial fires flickered along the sacred halls. Hot sticky beads of oil dripped down his bulky, impressive frame, as he slowly gravitated towards the door, shearing the floor with his impressive metallically augmented limbs.

Almost as if it were planned the low hum of liturgies constantly heard throughout the forge-city began to crescendo, crying out to the machine-spirit, further enhancing Cawl’s emotional state. It was almost as if Cawl’s own machine spirit was growing alongside the forge city, slowly building towards a great climax, but not yet, it was too soon.

The evening was young, there was more to – come.

Archmagos Dominus Belisarius Cawl crossed the threshold of the doorway, preparing for the long night ahead.

The Omnissiah’s Embrace – Part 2
- By Ryan Jones

For the first time he could remember, Archmagos Dominus Belisarius Cawl heard nothing but silence.

Cogitators whirred, nearby servo-skulls could be heard faintly humming through the corridors and the background magnificent machinery of Mars ever churned, but Cawl heard none of it.

For a moment, everything stopped.

Cawl could pin it down to the exact zeptosecond Thulia’s sacred robes laid bare on the floor. The same ones that appeared on the floor just a few metres in front of him. Still frozen, he accessed his memory banks to reassure himself what he just saw wasn’t a dream.

A frame forever frozen within the Archmagos’ mind was Thulia’s form as she crossed the threshold of the door, glimpsed once but forever engraved in the memory banks of the Archmagos.

He was alive.

Waves of golden red pieced through the ancient tapestries draped throughout the walkway, emanating towards the doorway, drawing him in. The burning of motor oil through the forge-city was thick in the air, enraging and disorientating. Compelled, lost of motor function Cawl stumbled forwards, trembling.

Despite Cawl’s natural form being long ago replaced by cybernetic augmentations his senses were overwhelmed. Heart thumping in his ears, nearby candescence blinded him as ancient raw industrial fires flickered along the sacred halls. Hot sticky beads of oil dripped down his bulky, impressive frame, as he slowly gravitated towards the door, shearing the floor with his impressive metallically augmented limbs.

Almost as if it were planned the low hum of liturgies constantly heard throughout the forge-city began to crescendo, crying out to the machine-spirit, further enhancing Cawl’s emotional state. It was almost as if Cawl’s own machine spirit was growing alongside the forge city, slowly building towards a great climax, but not yet, it was too soon.

The evening was young, there was more to – come.

Archmagos Dominus Belisarius Cawl crossed the threshold of the doorway, preparing for the long night ahead.
